reasons.existing: Best fidelity among the candidates: preserves the visible prose, punctuation, hyphenation, symbols, and mathematical expressions most accurately. It still omits the two visible algorithms and Figure 1 caption, begins mid-sentence, and includes text extending beyond the page.
reasons.docling: Contains most of the same prose in the correct reading order, but loses source hyphenation and spacing, weakens mathematical formatting, removes the hyphen in FedAvg-CSMC, and also omits the visible algorithms and caption. It additionally includes adjacent text beyond the page.
reasons.mineru_standard: Lowest fidelity. It begins later in the paragraph, omits more page content, truncates near the bottom of the visible page, and substantially corrupts mathematical notation through fragmented or incorrect LaTeX symbols and variables. The algorithms and caption are also missing.

reasons.existing: Best overall text and formula fidelity. Mathematical expressions, distributions, dimensions, sample-size functions, and constants remain semantically accurate despite being flattened into Unicode/plain text. Reading order is correct and the visible experimental prose is captured through the homogeneous-clients subsection. It omits the two algorithms and Figure 1 caption and begins mid-word.
reasons.docling: Close to existing in prose coverage and adds useful Markdown heading structure, but formula typography is less faithful: subscripts and superscripts are frequently flattened, arg max is collapsed, log n loses spacing, and the homogeneous-clients heading is concatenated with surrounding text. It also omits both algorithms and their caption and begins mid-word.
reasons.mineru_standard: Uses LaTeX markup, but introduces serious mathematical OCR errors, including spurious mathring, dots, tildes, altered variables, spaced operator names, malformed punctuation, and a badly corrupted N = 10K expression. It also omits more visible prose than the other candidates, stopping before the remainder of the experiment setup, and omits both algorithms and the caption.

Best overall preservation of the visible prose, caption structure, and mathematical notation. Equations retain LaTeX-style symbols, subscripts, hats, tildes, beta, and set notation more faithfully than the other excerpts. It preserves the figure caption, the continuation paragraph, and the adjacent section text in a coherent reading order. The main limitation is that the plotted regions are represented only as embedded-image placeholders, so chart labels and plotted text are not recoverable from the excerpt.
reasons.docling: Preserves most of the visible prose and reading order, including the figure caption and adjacent section text, but formula fidelity is weaker: hats, tildes, subscripts, and HTML entities are inconsistently represented. It also concatenates or damages some headings and words, such as the section heading and 'DoubleDescentunderDistributionShift'. The figure itself is reduced to a single image placeholder.
reasons.existing: Contains substantial visible-page text, including portions of plot labels, captions, and the continuation paragraph, but begins mid-content and has the least coherent coverage of the page. It omits or truncates important surrounding text, has weaker structure, and does not preserve the full figure organization or adjacent section content. Formula text is partly preserved but less consistently than mineru_standard.

Best page coverage and reading order. It preserves the visible (b) caption, textual plot labels and legends for row (c), the complete Figure 1 caption, and the body paragraph below the figure in approximately the correct sequence. Mathematical notation is mostly readable, including alpha, beta, 1/c = N/d, and the perturbed-test-data equation, but subscripts, hats, tildes, and R^d are flattened or imperfect.
reasons.docling: The main caption and body prose are largely accurate, but the page order is substantially wrong: the below-figure body paragraph appears before the (c) caption and Figure 1, while a section from the next page is appended. It omits the visible (b) caption and exposes almost none of the plot labels or legends. Formula accents and subscripts are represented inconsistently, and R^d is flattened.
reasons.mineru_standard: Preserves mathematical notation best, using structured LaTeX for beta, 1/c = N/d, R^d, X variables, hats, tildes, subscripts, and the perturbation equation. It also retains the Figure 1 caption and body text accurately. However, most plots are reduced to generic embedded-image placeholders, the (b) caption is only a truncated tail, and the reading order places the body text after the figure before adjacent next-page material without preserving all visible graph text.

reasons.existing: Best fidelity for the excerpted region. It preserves the displayed probability bound, SGD update equation, Theorem 6 bound, notation, reading order, headings, and surrounding prose accurately. However, it omits the visible beginning of the page and stops partway through the Representation Space Distribution Matching section, including formulas visible near the bottom.
reasons.docling: Text and section order are mostly recognizable, but all important displayed formulas are replaced by formula-not-decoded markers. It also removes mathematical spacing and punctuation in places, truncates before most of the visible lower-page content, and therefore has poor formula fidelity.
reasons.mineru_standard: Preserves several displayed formulas in LaTeX, including equation (3) and the SGD update, and covers more of the visible page than docling. However, it omits the actual Theorem 6 formula, introduces substantial notation and transcription errors, contains malformed LaTeX and bracket structure, misreads symbols and subscripts, and alters prose such as the KL-divergence sentence.

reasons.existing: Preserves most central prose and all three major mathematical statements, including equation (3), the SGD update, and Theorem 6. However, formulas are flattened into badly ordered text with displaced fractions, sums, subscripts, and superscripts, substantially reducing readability and Markdown fidelity. It also begins mid-paragraph, omitting the visible section heading and opening text, and truncates the representation-space discussion.
reasons.docling: Text and reading order are generally coherent, with useful heading structure and substantial prose coverage. However, every major displayed formula on the page is replaced by a formula-not-decoded placeholder, including equation (3), the SGD update, and Theorem 6. It also merges words around symbols and headings and truncates most of the representation-space section. Given the formula-first criterion, these omissions are decisive.
reasons.mineru_standard: Best overall preservation of the page's structure and displayed mathematics. Equation (3) and the SGD update are rendered as usable LaTeX with mostly correct fractions, sums, indices, and the equation tag. Headings and prose reading order are also preserved well. Defects include an erroneous vector accent on lambda, omission of the displayed Theorem 6 statement, malformed delimiters in the Markov-chain inequality, and several symbol corruptions such as dotted variables and D_ij. The lower representation-space content is truncated.

reasons.existing: Best fidelity on the visible page. It preserves the heading, reading order, prose, equation numbering, and the displayed formulas with substantially correct notation. It includes adjacent text from the preceding page and stops around line 250, omitting the visible equation (10) and subsequent paragraphs through line 269, so it is incomplete but accurate where present.
reasons.docling: Preserves much of the prose in approximately correct order, but begins mid-sentence, omits the section heading and all displayed formulas by replacing them with formula-not-decoded markers, and includes substantial text beyond the visible page. Formula fidelity is therefore very poor.
reasons.mineru_standard: Includes most of the visible page and renders equations in LaTeX, but introduces multiple substantive formula and text errors, including incorrect transformed-state definitions, altered matrices, notation substitutions, and a truncated ending. Its equation presentation is stronger than docling's, but mathematical fidelity is materially worse than existing.

Best fidelity. Preserves the complete Table 2 with correct row and column structure, headers, dataset groupings, values, captions, and dagger superscripts. The surrounding prose and section heading are also accurately represented, with only the excerpt ending before the full Table 3 caption and contents.
reasons.existing: Preserves the visible lower portion of Table 2 and the subsequent prose accurately, including most numerical values and the Table 3 content. However, it omits the Table 2 caption, headers, AudioSet rows, and much of the table structure by rendering it as aligned plain text. It also ends mid-sentence after the Table 3 discussion.
reasons.docling: Preserves the later prose and Table 3 reasonably well in Markdown, but Table 2 is severely incomplete and malformed: most of the table is omitted, text such as 'CAV-MAE(Gongetal.,2022b)' is corrupted, and table boundaries and alignment are unreliable. It also contains spacing and word-joining errors in surrounding text and ends prematurely.

Best overall because it preserves part of the table in a recognizable Markdown table structure and reproduces most of the visible prose. However, the table is severely incomplete, lacks its header and caption, and the text is truncated mid-section. Heading spacing and some formatting are also degraded.
reasons.mineru_standard: Provides the strongest continuous transcription of the visible prose, including section headings and most mathematical notation, but omits the entire table and caption. Several formulas contain OCR artifacts, including malformed fractions and an erroneous perturbation value.
reasons.existing: The prose is generally faithful, but it omits the table and caption entirely, begins partway through the page, and includes substantial text beyond the visible page, including the next-page figure caption. Reading order and page-boundary fidelity are therefore weaker.

Preserves the latter body text with high textual fidelity, including Sections 4.1 and 4.2, but omits the entire table, its caption, the Hardness Manipulations paragraph, and the beginning of the evaluation protocol. It also includes substantial adjacent-page text.
reasons.docling: Preserves a small tail of the table as Markdown and most text from Hardness Manipulations through part of Section 4.1. However, nearly all table rows and headers are missing, the full caption is omitted, the Section 4.1 heading loses word spacing, fractions are flattened, and the page ending including Section 4.2 is absent.
reasons.mineru_standard: Best overall page coverage and reading order: it retains the caption ending, Hardness Manipulations, the full evaluation protocol, all of Section 4.1, and the start of Section 4.2. Headings and most prose are well preserved. The principal failure is complete omission of the table and most of its caption; mathematical fractions are structured but contain artifacts such as spaced digits, a stray arrow, and a quoted numerator.

Best overall preservation. It maintains the reading order of the figure caption and surrounding prose, represents Table 4 as a complete table, and preserves the visible multi-level structure and values of Table 5 using HTML table markup. However, the excerpt is truncated during the Table 5 rows and omits the lower-page Section 4.2 text.
reasons.docling: Preserves the prose and complete Table 4 accurately, and converts Table 5 into a structured Markdown table with correct grouped columns. However, it places Table 4 after a continuation of the surrounding paragraph, disrupts reading order, omits nearly all Table 5 data after the header, and has minor header fidelity issues such as 'F1Score' and 'AUCScore'.
reasons.existing: Text is mostly faithful and includes the complete Table 4 values, but both tables are flattened into spatially interleaved text rather than preserved structurally. Table 5 is incomplete and truncated mid-row, and the excerpt includes unrelated preceding text and a page-number separator.

Preserves the figure caption, surrounding prose, all of Table 4's values, and several rows of Table 5. However, Table 4 is interleaved with the paragraph because the two-column reading order was not resolved, and both tables are represented as fragile whitespace-aligned text rather than semantic tables. Table 5 is truncated during the X3D row, and the lower section of the page is omitted.
reasons.docling: Produces clean prose in logical reading order and an accurate semantic Markdown representation of Table 4. It also reconstructs Table 5's grouped column headers well, but the excerpt ends before preserving any Table 5 data rows. The stray '(r)' is an extraction artifact, and the figure itself and the lower page section are absent.
reasons.mineru_standard: Best overall fidelity. It preserves the figure as an embedded image marker, accurately captures the caption and prose in logical reading order, renders Table 4 as a correct Markdown table, and retains Table 5's multi-level grouped headers using appropriate row and column spans. It also preserves more Table 5 data than docling, though the excerpt truncates during the Slowfast row and omits the lower page section.

Best overall preservation of the visible table through structured HTML rows and cells, followed by mostly faithful section text in the correct reading order. It still omits the table header and earlier rows, begins with a fragment from the preceding table content, truncates the page near the end of section 5.3, and contains minor formatting errors such as 'chainof-thought'.
reasons.docling: Preserves part of the table and includes the main body text in the correct order, but the table excerpt is incomplete and malformed, with missing headers and an incorrectly formatted row. Text fidelity is generally good but has spacing and hyphenation errors, and the excerpt extends into adjacent content and is truncated.
reasons.existing: Body text is comparatively faithful and covers the visible discussion, but it omits the entire table, begins mid-sentence, and includes substantial adjacent-page text. This makes it substantially weaker for the page-level structure and table-preservation requirements.

Omits Table 1 entirely, including its caption, headers, group labels, and all numeric results. It also begins mid-sentence, losing the section heading and opening of the results discussion. The remaining prose is generally faithful and in reading order, but it includes substantial adjacent-page text.
reasons.docling: Preserves only the final part of Table 1, and that fragment has malformed Markdown structure, including merged values such as '54.7 53.3' in one cell. The main prose and section ordering are mostly correct, but there are fidelity defects such as 'ToMQAs', 'GPT4', 'ADDITIONALEVALUATION', and 'chainof-thought'. It also includes adjacent-page material.
reasons.mineru_standard: Best table preservation among the candidates: the visible tail of Table 1 is represented as structured HTML with correct row and cell values, although the excerpt still omits most of the table, its caption, headers, and group labels. The page prose, headings, emphasis, punctuation, and reading order are highly faithful. Minor defects include the clipped initial table row and 'chainof-thought', and the excerpt truncates the final paragraph visible on the page.
